images.title: 3 m is 300 cm on a double number line
images.purpose: Show one length with two names on a double number line: the top line in m, the bottom line in cm, the arrow x100, and the two lengths of the example, 3 m = 300 cm and 450 cm = 4 m 50 cm.
images.composition: Two parallel number lines with six ticks each, an arrow x100 on the left, a teal marker at 3 m and an amber marker at 450 cm.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TOP LINE: one horizontal line from x 228 to x 1228 at y 260 with exactly 6 tall tick marks (44 px) at x 228, 428, 628, 828, 1028 and 1228, labelled above in 44 px bold 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, and the unit m written at the right end, x 1290, y 260. BOTTOM LINE: one horizontal line from x 228 to x 1228 at y 500 with exactly 6 tall tick marks at the same x positions, labelled below in 44 px bold 0, 100, 200, 300, 400 and 500, and the unit cm written at the right end, x 1290, y 500. ARROW: one curved arrow on the left, from the top line at x 180 down to the bottom line at x 180, with the label ×100 in a grey #6B7280 rounded box 120 by 56 px beside it (x 90 to 210, y 350 to 406). MARKERS: a teal #0072B2 dot (24 px) on the top line at 3 (x 828) and on the bottom line at 300 (x 828) joined by a thin vertical teal line, with the label 3 m = 300 cm in 40 px at x 828, y 600; an amber #E69F00 dot (24 px) on the bottom line at 450 (x 1128) with the label 450 cm = 4 m 50 cm in 40 px at x 1128, y 680. In all: 2 number lines, 12 tall ticks, 3 dots, 1 arrow. All shapes are flat fills with thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (3 px), no shadows and no gradients; all text is dark #1F2937 sans-serif. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 6 ticks on either line
a label on a tick other than those listed
images.takeaway: 1 m = 100 cm, so m become cm when you multiply by 100.
images.description: A double number line with m on the top line, cm on the bottom line and the arrow ×100, showing 3 m = 300 cm and 450 cm = 4 m 50 cm.
images.context: Concept image for Metres and Centimetres: One Length, Two Names. It follows the idea of the double number line in your maths book (100 cm over 1 m with the arrows ×2 and ×100) and shows the concept's own example of 3 m and 450 cm.
images.teaching_notes: Slide along the lines with the child: each tick on the top line sits over the tick that is 100 times bigger. The slip to watch: reading 450 cm as 4 m 5 cm.
